```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Jaber_2023_cyclophosphamide"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Jaber_2023_cyclophosphamide"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.2144> (open access, PMC10087276)

The supporting information holds the final NONMEM control stream (whose
`$THETA` and `$OMEGA` blocks carry the final estimates of Table 2 to more
digits), the Julia simulation script behind Table 3 and Figures S2-S4, and
Figures S1-S4. A literature check on 2026-10-26 (Europe PMC) found no erratum
or correction for this article.

Only phosphoramide mustard (PM) was measured. Cyclophosphamide and
4-hydroxycyclophosphamide enter the model as two amount-only transit
compartments that share one rate constant and serve only to delay the
appearance of PM; the authors caution that this rate constant should not be
interpreted mechanistically. Because the fraction of the cyclophosphamide dose
converted to PM is not identifiable, the PM clearance, volume and Vmax are
apparent values scaled by that fraction.

# Population

Jaber 2023 analysed 85 of 110 adults enrolled in a single-centre observational
PK study at the University of Minnesota. All had a high-risk hematologic
malignancy (leukemia 49%, myelodysplastic syndrome 19%, lymphoma 11%, other
21%) and received a reduced-intensity conditioning regimen for allogeneic
hematopoietic cell transplantation: a single dose of cyclophosphamide 50 mg/kg
infused over 2 h on day -7, fludarabine on days -6 to -2 and 200 cGy total
body irradiation on day -1. The dose was based on total body weight, or on
adjusted body weight for patients whose weight exceeded 150% of ideal body
weight (28%). Median age was 63 years (21-75), median weight 84 kg (47-177),
45% were female and median Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance was 77 mL/min
(32-150) (Table 1). PM was sampled at 0, 4, 6, 8, 23, 26 and 47 h after the
start of the infusion; 506 concentrations were analysed, 11.4% of them below
the 50 ng/mL limit of quantification.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Jaber_2023_cyclophosphamide")()$population`.

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Jaber_2023_cyclophosphamide.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl_renal` (renal clearance, 70 kg, CrCL 85 mL/min) | log(14.9) L/h | Table 2; NONMEM `$THETA(1)` 14.913 |
| `lvc` (apparent volume, 70 kg) | log(525) L | Table 2; `$THETA(2)` 524.657 |
| `lktr` (shared transit rate constant, 70 kg) | log(1.3) 1/h | Table 2; `$THETA(3)` 1.30505 |
| `lvmax` (Michaelis-Menten Vmax, 70 kg) | log(81.2) mg/h | Table 2; `$THETA(7)` 81.2164 |
| `lkm` (Michaelis-Menten Km) | log(0.51) mg/L | Table 2; `$THETA(8)` 0.514354 |
| `e_crcl_cl_renal` | 1 (held constant) | Methods after Equation 3 (estimated 0.97, then set to 1); Table 2; `$THETA(4) 1 FIX` |
| `e_wt_cl_renal`, `e_wt_vmax` | 0.75 (held constant) | Equations 3-4; Table 2 |
| `e_wt_vc` | 1 (held constant) | Methods "Theory-based allometry"; Table 2 |
| `e_wt_ktr` | 0.25 (held constant) | Equation 2; Table 2 |
| `etalcl_renal`, `etalvc`, `etalktr`, `etalkm` | 0.15861, 0.108285, 0.0744403, 0.0842706 | NONMEM `$OMEGA`; Table 2 BSV 39.8, 32.9, 27.3, 29.0% (= 100 x sqrt(omega^2)) |
| `propSd`, `addSd` | 0.097, 54.9 ng/mL | Table 2; `$THETA(5)`, `$THETA(6)`; `$ERROR` SD = sqrt(PROP^2 + ADD^2) |
| Cockcroft-Gault CrCL, female factor 0.85, cap at 150 mL/min | n/a | Methods "Model Development"; NONMEM `$PK` |
| Renal clearance `cl_renal = CL * ((CrCL/85) * (70/WT))^1 * (WT/70)^0.75` | n/a | Equation 3; NONMEM `$PK` |
| Metabolic elimination `vmax * C / (km + C)` | n/a | Equations 4-6; NONMEM `$DES` |
| `d/dt(depot_iv)`, `d/dt(transit1)`, `d/dt(central)` | n/a | Equations 7-9; NONMEM `$DES` (A(1), A(3), A(2)) |
| `Cc = central / vc * 1000` (ng/mL) | n/a | NONMEM `$PK` `S2 = V/1000` |

# Virtual cohort

The original data are not public. The cohort below approximates Table 1. Age,
weight and serum creatinine are drawn so the derived Cockcroft-Gault creatinine
clearance spans roughly the observed range; height is drawn only to decide
which patients are dosed on adjusted body weight.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20230101)
n_sub <- 200

cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 0.45),
  AGE = pmin(pmax(round(rnorm(n_sub, 60, 11)), 21), 75),
  WT = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n_sub, log(84), 0.22)), 47), 177),
  CREAT = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n_sub, log(1.1), 0.25)), 0.4), 2.0),
  HT_cm = ifelse(SEXF == 1, rnorm(n_sub, 163, 7), rnorm(n_sub, 177, 7))
) |>
  mutate(
    # Devine ideal body weight; adjusted body weight when WT > 150% of IBW
    # (Jaber 2023 Equation 1).
    IBW = ifelse(SEXF == 1, 45.5, 50) + 2.3 * (HT_cm / 2.54 - 60),
    adjusted = WT > 1.5 * IBW,
    dose_wt = ifelse(adjusted, IBW + 0.5 * (WT - IBW), WT),
    amt = 50 * dose_wt,
    crcl = pmin((140 - AGE) * WT / (72 * CREAT) * 0.85^SEXF, 150)
  )

cohort |>
  summarise(
    `Age median (range)` = sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", median(AGE), min(AGE), max(AGE)),
    `Weight median (range), kg` = sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", median(WT), min(WT), max(WT)),
    `Female, %` = sprintf("%.0f", 100 * mean(SEXF)),
    `CrCL median (range), mL/min` = sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", median(crcl), min(crcl), max(crcl)),
    `Dosed on adjusted weight, %` = sprintf("%.0f", 100 * mean(adjusted))
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Characteristic", values_to = "Virtual cohort") |>
  mutate(`Jaber 2023 Table 1` = c("63 (21-75)", "84 (47-177)", "45", "77 (32-150)", "28")) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Virtual cohort against Table 1.")
```

Every patient receives one 2-h infusion of cyclophosphamide 50 mg/kg into
`depot_iv`. Observations are on the PM state `central`; the model returns the
PM concentration `Cc` (ng/mL) at those rows.

```{r events}
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 100, by = 0.5), 4, 6, 8, 23, 26, 47)))

dose_rows <- cohort |>
  transmute(id, time = 0, amt, dur = 2, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot_iv",
            SEXF, AGE, WT, CREAT)
obs_rows <- cohort |>
  select(id, SEXF, AGE, WT, CREAT) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
  mutate(amt = 0, dur = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
events <- bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  mutate(treatment = "CY 50 mg/kg")
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[events$evid == 0, c("id", "time")]))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Jaber_2023_cyclophosphamide")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("treatment", "WT")) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure S1: observed PM concentrations

Figure S1 of Jaber 2023 plots the 506 observed PM concentrations. The
simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of the virtual cohort (with residual
error) at the protocol sampling times should cover that cloud: most early
(4-8 h) observations lie between about 2,500 and 9,000 ng/mL and most 23-26 h
observations between the 50 ng/mL limit of quantification and about
2,500 ng/mL.

```{r figure-s1}
set.seed(20230102)
sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events |> filter(evid == 1 | time %in% c(4, 6, 8, 23, 26, 47)),
  keep = c("treatment")
) |>
  as.data.frame()

vpc <- sim_vpc |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), Q50 = quantile(sim, 0.50), Q95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(vpc, digits = 0,
             caption = "Simulated PM concentration percentiles (ng/mL) at the sampling times.")

ggplot(vpc, aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(Q05, 1), ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 50, colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Time after start of infusion (h)", y = "PM concentration (ng/mL)",
       title = "Simulated 5th-50th-95th percentiles with residual error",
       caption = "Compare with Figure S1 of Jaber 2023; red line is the 50 ng/mL LLOQ.")

# The early median sits in the middle of the Figure S1 cloud and the 23 h
# median well below the early peak; a mis-scaled volume or dose moves both by
# tens of percent.
early_med <- vpc$Q50[vpc$time == 6]
late_med <- vpc$Q50[vpc$time == 23]
stopifnot(early_med > 3000, early_med < 7500, late_med > 300, late_med < 2500)
```

## Figure S3 and Table 3: effect of creatinine clearance on PM exposure

The paper's sensitivity analysis uses a 70-kg typical patient who receives
3,500 mg of cyclophosphamide (50 mg/kg), with creatinine clearance set
directly to 30-120 mL/min. In the supplementary Julia script the whole dose is
placed in the cyclophosphamide compartment at time zero, rather than infused
over 2 h, so the replication does the same. In this model creatinine
clearance is computed from serum creatinine, so the serum creatinine that
gives each target clearance is back-calculated for a 63-year-old man.

```{r typical-setup}
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
target_crcl <- seq(30, 120, by = 10)

typical_events <- function(crcl_target, end = 100) {
  rxode2::et(amt = 3500, cmt = "depot_iv") |>
    rxode2::et(seq(0, end, by = 0.05), cmt = "central") |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(id = crcl_target, WT = 70, AGE = 63, SEXF = 0,
           CREAT = (140 - 63) * 70 / (72 * crcl_target))
}
typ_ev <- bind_rows(lapply(target_crcl, typical_events))

trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)

solve_typical <- function(vmax_mg_h) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, events = typ_ev,
                  params = c(lvmax = log(vmax_mg_h))) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    rename(crcl_target = id) |>
    mutate(crcl_target = as.numeric(as.character(crcl_target)))
}
sim_typ <- solve_typical(81.2)
```

```{r figure-s3}
fig_s3 <- sim_typ |>
  filter(crcl_target %in% c(30, 60, 120), time <= 48) |>
  group_by(crcl_target) |>
  arrange(time, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(auc = c(0, cumsum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2))) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(fig_s3, aes(time, auc, colour = factor(crcl_target))) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 48, 8)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "PM AUC (ng*h/mL)", colour = "CrCL (mL/min)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure S3 of Jaber 2023.")

auc48 <- fig_s3 |>
  group_by(crcl_target) |>
  summarise(auc48 = max(auc), .groups = "drop") |>
  # Plateau values read by the maintainers from Figure S3.
  mutate(figure_s3 = c(`30` = 122000, `60` = 100500, `120` = 75000)[as.character(crcl_target)],
         pct_diff = 100 * (auc48 / figure_s3 - 1))
knitr::kable(auc48, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 1),
             caption = "AUC0-48 h of the typical 70-kg patient against Figure S3.")
# Deterministic typical-value solve against a figure read to about 1%.
stopifnot(all(abs(auc48$pct_diff) < 4))
```

Table 3 reports the percentage increase in AUC0-8 h and in AUC0-100 h
(approximately AUC to infinity) relative to a creatinine clearance of
120 mL/min. The table below compares Table 3 with the model as published
(Vmax 81.2 mg/h) and with the same model at Vmax 40.2 mg/h, the value written
into the supplementary Julia function that generated Table 3.

```{r table-3}
pct_increase <- function(sims) {
  sims |>
    group_by(crcl_target) |>
    summarise(auc8 = trap(time[time <= 8], Cc[time <= 8]),
              auc100 = trap(time, Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(inc8 = 100 * (auc8 / auc8[crcl_target == 120] - 1),
           inc100 = 100 * (auc100 / auc100[crcl_target == 120] - 1))
}
published_t3 <- tibble(
  crcl_target = target_crcl,
  t3_inc8 = c(10.4, 9.2, 8.0, 6.8, 5.6, 4.4, 3.3, 2.1, 1.1, 0),
  t3_inc100 = c(102.3, 80.9, 63.9, 49.9, 38.2, 28.3, 19.7, 12.3, 5.8, 0)
)
t3 <- pct_increase(sim_typ) |>
  select(crcl_target, inc8, inc100) |>
  left_join(pct_increase(solve_typical(40.2)) |>
              select(crcl_target, inc8_v40 = inc8, inc100_v40 = inc100),
            by = "crcl_target") |>
  left_join(published_t3, by = "crcl_target")

t3 |>
  select(crcl_target, t3_inc8, inc8, t3_inc100, inc100, inc100_v40) |>
  rename(
    "CrCL (mL/min)" = crcl_target,
    "Table 3 AUC0-8 increase (%)" = t3_inc8,
    "Model AUC0-8 increase (%)" = inc8,
    "Table 3 AUC increase (%)" = t3_inc100,
    "Model AUC increase (%), Vmax 81.2" = inc100,
    "AUC increase (%), Vmax 40.2" = inc100_v40
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Table 3 of Jaber 2023 against the packaged model.")

# AUC0-8 h hardly depends on Vmax, and the model reproduces the Table 3
# column to rounding. The total-AUC column is reproduced to rounding only at
# Vmax 40.2 mg/h; that it is NOT reproduced at the published Vmax is the
# documented deviation below, so the published-Vmax total AUC is not gated.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(t3$inc8 - t3$t3_inc8) < 0.25),
  all(abs(t3$inc100_v40 - t3$t3_inc100) < 0.25)
)
```

## Figures S2 and S4: elimination routes

The renal (linear) and metabolic (Michaelis-Menten) elimination rates are
integrated over 0-100 h for the same typical patient.

```{r figure-s4}
routes <- sim_typ |>
  group_by(crcl_target) |>
  summarise(
    renal = trap(time, kel * central),
    metabolic = trap(time, vmax * cpm_mgl / (km + cpm_mgl)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_renal = 100 * renal / 3500, pct_metabolic = 100 * metabolic / 3500)

# Percent renal at the five plotted CrCL values, read by the maintainers from
# Figure S4.
fig_s4 <- tibble(crcl_target = c(30, 50, 80, 100, 120),
                 figure_s4_renal = c(18.5, 27, 36, 41, 45))
s4 <- inner_join(routes, fig_s4, by = "crcl_target")
s4 |>
  select(crcl_target, figure_s4_renal, pct_renal, pct_metabolic) |>
  rename("CrCL (mL/min)" = crcl_target,
         "Figure S4 renal (%)" = figure_s4_renal,
         "Model renal (%)" = pct_renal,
         "Model metabolic (%)" = pct_metabolic) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Share of the dose eliminated by each route against Figure S4.")
stopifnot(all(abs(s4$pct_renal - s4$figure_s4_renal) < 2))

routes |>
  select(crcl_target, Renal = pct_renal, `Non-renal` = pct_metabolic) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-crcl_target, names_to = "route", values_to = "pct") |>
  ggplot(aes(crcl_target, pct, colour = route)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(x = "CrCL (mL/min)", y = "Dose eliminated (%)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure S4 of Jaber 2023.")
```

```{r figure-s2}
sim_typ |>
  filter(crcl_target %in% c(30, 60, 120)) |>
  group_by(crcl_target) |>
  arrange(time, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(eliminated = c(0, cumsum(diff(time) * (
    head(kel * central + vmax * cpm_mgl / (km + cpm_mgl), -1) +
      tail(kel * central + vmax * cpm_mgl / (km + cpm_mgl), -1)) / 2))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ggplot(aes(time, eliminated, colour = factor(crcl_target))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 3500, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Cumulative amount eliminated (mg)", colour = "CrCL (mL/min)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure S2 of Jaber 2023.")
```

# PKNCA validation

NCA on the dense simulated profiles of the virtual cohort (with between-subject
variability, without residual error). The paper reports no NCA table. Its
Discussion places the PM AUC0-8 h threshold for higher nonrelapse mortality,
34,235 ng*h/mL from the authors' earlier analysis of this cohort, at about 20%
above the median, which implies a cohort median AUC0-8 h of roughly
28,500 ng*h/mL; that derived value is the only reference available.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
stopifnot(all(tapply(sim_nca$time, sim_nca$id, min) == 0))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, dur, treatment)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, duration = "dur")

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 0),
  end = c(8, Inf),
  auclast = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  cmax = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  tmax = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  aucinf.obs = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  half.life = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca_res)
```

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tibble(treatment = "CY 50 mg/kg", auclast = 34235 / 1.2)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(auclast = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated median AUC0-8 h against the value implied by the Discussion. * differs by >20%.")

auc08 <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast", end == 8)
# Centre-based check: the cohort median AUC0-8 h lies within 25% of the
# implied 28,500 ng*h/mL.
stopifnot(abs(median(auc08$PPORRES) / (34235 / 1.2) - 1) < 0.25)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Table 3 (and the abstract's 80.9% figure) do not follow from the published
  Vmax.** With the Table 2 estimate Vmax = 81.2 mg/h, the typical 70-kg patient
  reproduces the AUC0-48 h curves of Figure S3 and the renal share of
  elimination in Figure S4 to within the reading precision of the figures, and
  the AUC0-8 h column of Table 3 to rounding. The total-AUC column of Table 3 is
  reproduced to rounding only with Vmax = 40.2 mg/h, the value hard-coded in
  the `renal_fn` function of the supplementary Julia script (its `exposure`
  function, used for Figures S2 and S3, uses 81.2). At the published Vmax, a
  fall in creatinine clearance from 120 to 40 mL/min raises total PM AUC by
  about 53%, not 80.9%. The model keeps the estimated Vmax of 81.2 mg/h, which
  Table 2, the abstract and the NONMEM `$THETA` all report.
- **Bolus versus infusion in the sensitivity simulations.** The paper's Methods
  describe the sensitivity analysis as a 2-h infusion, but the supplementary
  Julia script places the dose in the cyclophosphamide compartment at time
  zero. The replications above follow the script. The infusion lowers AUC0-8 h
  by about 14% and changes the percentage increases by at most 1.5
  percentage points.
- **Creatinine clearance is computed inside the model** from `AGE`, `WT`,
  `CREAT` (mg/dL) and `SEXF` with the Cockcroft-Gault equation and capped at
  150 mL/min, as in the NONMEM `$PK` block, rather than read as a column. To
  impose a creatinine clearance directly, set
  `CREAT = (140 - AGE) * WT * 0.85^SEXF / (72 * CrCL)`.
- **Below-quantification data** were fit with the M3 method in the source
  analysis; a simulation model has no censoring, so simulated values below
  50 ng/mL are returned as they are.
- **Virtual cohort.** Age, weight, serum creatinine and height distributions
  were chosen by the maintainers to approximate Table 1; the paper does not
  report serum creatinine or height, nor which ideal-body-weight formula set
  the adjusted-weight dosing (the Devine formula is used here).
- **Typical patient for the sensitivity analysis.** The paper fixes weight at
  70 kg and sets creatinine clearance directly; the age of 63 years used to
  back-calculate serum creatinine has no effect on the result.
